extracted.intended_audience: policy advocates, journalists, consumer protection advocates, and the general public interested in broadband/FCC rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Summarizing an enforcement action and investigation into companies that supplied fabricated public comments to influence an FCC proceeding (net neutrality repeal). Focus is on identifying deceptive practices in notice-and-comment campaigns and their consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity of commenter identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Fake comments used the identities of millions of consumers, including thousands of New Yorkers, without their knowledge or consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments must reflect the genuine identity and informed consent of the person whose name/email/address is used. Submitting comments that impersonate real people or use identifying information without consent is deceptive and subject to investigation and enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine consumer participation (no fabrication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead generators hired to enroll consumers instead simply fabricated consumers' responses rather than collecting real opt-ins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice-and-comment submissions should be produced by actual individuals who knowingly participated; methods must verify opt-in and avoid producing automated, fabricated, or proxy responses. Anti-pattern: substituting fabricated responses for real consumer input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency about who paid for/comment campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: The nation’s largest broadband companies funded a secret campaign to generate millions of comments to the FCC in 2017.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizers and funders of large-scale comment drives should disclose their involvement; undisclosed, covert funding that misrepresents public sentiment undermines the integrity of the rulemaking process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper use of lead generation tactics and incentives
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead generators used advertisements and prizes, like gift cards and sweepstakes entries, to encourage consumers to join the campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While recruitment incentives may be used to solicit participation, they must not be used as a pretext for producing fabricated submissions; recruitment processes should include verifiable consent and clear disclosure of purpose and funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement and documentation of scope and impact of abusive practices
rubrics_metrics.description: The OAG investigation found more than 8.5 million fake comments submitted to the FCC and more than half a million fake letters sent to Congress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations should quantify the scale of fabricated input to assess the extent of misrepresentation in the rulemaking record; accurate documentation supports enforcement and corrective measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement consequences for supplying fake comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Collectively, the three companies have agreed to pay $615,000 in penalties and disgorgement; this follows prior agreements in related investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities that supply fabricated comments may face civil enforcement including monetary penalties and disgorgement; enforcement history and settlements are relevant precedents when evaluating risk and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition / importance of the underlying policy issue (contextual standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: Net neutrality prohibits broadband providers from blocking, slowing down, or charging companies to prioritize certain content on the internet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding the substantive regulatory issue at stake (here, net neutrality) is important for assessing why manipulation of the notice-and-comment process is consequential to public policy outcomes.
